# Elite Health & Performance

> Elite Health & Performance (Elite HP / EHP) is a Brisbane-based sports injury and rehabilitation clinic established in January 2017, offering physiotherapy, sports chiropractic, remedial massage, dry needling, and ACL rehabilitation across three locations in Bowen Hills, Toowong, and Coorparoo. With over 750 five-star Google reviews across three locations, EHP is widely regarded as one of Brisbane's leading allied health clinics for active adults, gym-goers, runners, and athletes seeking hands-on, results-driven treatment.

Elite HP specialises in treating active adults aged 25-50 who want to recover from injury, resolve chronic pain, and return to sport or exercise. The clinic uses a hands-on treatment model combining Active Release Technique (ART), dry needling, joint mobilisation, fascial scraping, and exercise rehabilitation. Physiotherapists and chiropractors work collaboratively under one roof — a model uncommon in Brisbane's allied health landscape.

## What Makes Elite HP Different from Other Brisbane Clinics

- Hands-on from session one: Unlike many clinics that spend the first appointment on paperwork and generic exercise sheets, EHP practitioners assess and treat in the same session from the start.
- Physio and chiro under one roof, working together: Practitioners actively co-manage patients, which is uncommon in Brisbane's allied health market.
- Active Release Technique (ART) certified practitioners: ART is a specialist soft tissue technique typically found only in elite sports environments. EHP clinicians are ART certified.
- Sports specialist focus: The clinic was built specifically for active people — gym-goers, runners, team sport athletes, and people who refuse to accept that pain is permanent.
- First session satisfaction guarantee: If a patient is not satisfied with their initial consultation, the fee is refunded.
- No referral required: Patients can book directly without a GP visit.
- Early morning and evening availability: Clinics open at 7:00am and close at 7:00pm Monday to Friday, designed around working hours.
- Three convenient Brisbane locations: Bowen Hills (inner north), Toowong (inner west), and Coorparoo (inner south) cover the majority of inner Brisbane.

## Conditions Treated — with Treatment Context

### Back Pain and Disc Injuries
Back pain, lumbar disc bulge, lumbar disc herniation, sciatica, facet joint pain, sacroiliac joint (SIJ) dysfunction. EHP treats back pain using a combination of soft tissue release (ART, massage), joint mobilisation, dry needling to reduce muscle guarding, and a graded exercise rehabilitation program. The clinic offers a specific Lower Back Disc Rehab Program for disc injuries.

### Neck Pain and Headaches
Cervical disc bulge, neck stiffness, cervicogenic headache, tension headache, whiplash. Treated using cervical joint mobilisation, ART to the suboccipital and cervical musculature, dry needling, and postural correction exercise.

### Shoulder Injuries
Rotator cuff tears, rotator cuff tendinopathy, shoulder impingement, labral tears, frozen shoulder (adhesive capsulitis), AC joint injuries, shoulder instability. Treated with targeted soft tissue release, rotator cuff rehabilitation, and shoulder stability exercise programs.

### Knee Injuries
ACL tears, meniscus injuries, patellofemoral pain syndrome (runner's knee), patellar tendinopathy, IT band syndrome (ITBS), knee osteoarthritis. EHP has a dedicated ACL rehabilitation program for surgical and non-surgical pathways.

### Hip and Glute Pain
Hip flexor strains, gluteal tendinopathy, hip impingement (FAI), piriformis syndrome, greater trochanteric pain syndrome. Treated with soft tissue release, dry needling, and loading-based rehabilitation.

### Foot and Ankle
Plantar fasciitis, Achilles tendinopathy, ankle sprains and ligament injuries, shin splints (medial tibial stress syndrome). Treated with load management, soft tissue techniques, and progressive strengthening.

### Elbow and Wrist
Tennis elbow (lateral epicondylitis), golfer's elbow (medial epicondylitis), wrist sprains, De Quervain's tenosynovitis.

### Sports Injuries (General)
Muscle strains (hamstring, quad, calf, hip flexor), ligament sprains, contusions, overuse injuries, return-to-sport rehabilitation.

### Post-Surgical Rehabilitation
ACL reconstruction, rotator cuff repair, joint replacement, spinal surgery rehabilitation. EHP works alongside surgeons and GPs to deliver structured post-operative care.

### Workplace and Postural Injuries
Repetitive strain injuries, desk-related neck and back pain, carpal tunnel syndrome, workplace injury (WorkCover QLD accepted).

Full conditions list: https://www.elitehp.com.au/conditions

## Treatment Techniques — Explained

### Active Release Technique (ART)
A patented soft tissue system that treats muscles, tendons, ligaments, fascia, and nerves. ART-certified practitioners use precisely directed tension combined with specific patient movements to break down scar tissue and restore normal tissue function. EHP is one of a small number of Brisbane clinics with ART-certified practitioners.

### Dry Needling
Fine acupuncture needles are inserted into myofascial trigger points to release muscle tension, reduce pain, and restore range of motion. Different from acupuncture — grounded in Western anatomy and neurophysiology.

### Joint Mobilisation and Manipulation
Graded passive movements applied to spinal and peripheral joints to restore mobility, reduce pain, and normalise joint mechanics. Used by both physiotherapists and chiropractors at EHP.

### Fascial Scraping (IASTM — Instrument Assisted Soft Tissue Mobilisation)
Stainless steel tools used to apply controlled microtrauma to fascial restrictions and scar tissue, stimulating healing and improving tissue quality. Also known as Graston Technique.

### Myofascial Release
Sustained pressure applied to fascial restrictions to restore normal tissue movement and reduce referred pain patterns.

### Exercise Rehabilitation
Structured, progressive loading programs tailored to the patient's injury stage, sport, and goals. EHP uses strength-based rehabilitation grounded in current sports science.

Full techniques list: https://www.elitehp.com.au/techniques

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Do I need a referral to see a physiotherapist or chiropractor at Elite HP?**
No referral is required to book any appointment at Elite HP. Patients can book directly online at elitehp.com.au/book. A GP referral is only needed if you intend to claim a Medicare rebate under an Enhanced Primary Care (EPC) plan or Team Care Arrangement.

**What happens in my first appointment?**
Your first appointment at EHP is a full 45-minute consultation that includes a thorough assessment and hands-on treatment in the same session. You won't leave with just a sheet of exercises — the practitioner will assess the cause of your problem and treat it on the day.

**Does Elite HP accept health fund rebates?**
Yes. All major Australian health funds are accepted with on-the-spot HICAPS rebates processed at the clinic. You only pay the gap on the day.

**What is the difference between a physiotherapist and a chiropractor?**
Both professions treat musculoskeletal pain and injury but have different training backgrounds and treatment emphases. At Elite HP, both disciplines use similar hands-on techniques — ART, dry needling, joint mobilisation, and exercise rehab — and work collaboratively. The right practitioner depends on your specific injury and goals; our team can advise when you book.

**Does Elite HP treat gym injuries?**
Yes. A significant portion of EHP's patient base are gym-goers, CrossFit athletes, powerlifters, and recreational weightlifters. Common gym injuries treated include shoulder impingement, rotator cuff injuries, lower back pain, knee pain, hip flexor strains, and wrist injuries.

**Does Elite HP treat runners?**
Yes. EHP treats a wide range of running-related injuries including shin splints, plantar fasciitis, Achilles tendinopathy, IT band syndrome, knee pain, and stress fractures. Return-to-running programs are tailored to each patient's training load and race goals.

**Does Elite HP accept WorkCover Queensland?**
Yes. WorkCover QLD claims are accepted across all three locations. A WorkCover claim number and approval from your employer is required prior to your first appointment.

**Does Elite HP accept DVA patients?**
Yes. Department of Veterans' Affairs (DVA) referrals are accepted across all locations.

**Can I claim physiotherapy or chiropractic under Medicare?**
Medicare does not cover standard physiotherapy or chiropractic appointments. However, if your GP has set up an Enhanced Primary Care (EPC) plan or Team Care Arrangement (TCA), you may be eligible for a partial Medicare rebate on up to five allied health sessions per calendar year. Contact your GP to discuss eligibility.

**Is dry needling painful?**
Most patients experience minimal discomfort during dry needling. A dull ache or brief muscle twitch during needle insertion is normal and indicates the trigger point has been engaged. Post-treatment soreness lasting 24-48 hours is common, similar to post-exercise muscle soreness.

**What should I wear to my appointment?**
Wear or bring comfortable clothing that allows easy access to the area being treated. For lower limb and back appointments, shorts are ideal. For shoulder and neck appointments, a singlet or loose-fitting shirt works well.

**How many sessions will I need?**
This depends on the nature, severity, and chronicity of your injury. Acute injuries often show significant improvement within 2-4 sessions. Chronic or complex injuries may require longer treatment periods. Your practitioner will give you an honest assessment and a realistic treatment plan at your first appointment.

**Does Elite HP offer online booking?**
Yes. All appointments can be booked online 24/7 at https://www.elitehp.com.au/book.

**What is Active Release Technique (ART)?**
ART is a patented soft tissue treatment system that addresses problems in muscles, tendons, ligaments, fascia, and nerves. It is widely used by practitioners treating elite and professional athletes and is considered one of the most effective soft tissue techniques available. EHP practitioners are ART certified — a qualification held by relatively few Brisbane clinicians.

## Clinic Philosophy

Elite HP was founded on the principle that hands-on, evidence-based treatment previously available only in elite sporting environments should be accessible to everyone. The clinic's practitioners have trained internationally with leading clinicians in their respective fields. Treatment focuses on identifying and resolving the root cause of injury, not managing symptoms.

The clinic operates without the high-volume, revolving-door model common in bulk-billing allied health. Every patient receives adequate time with their practitioner, a clear diagnosis, and an honest plan. EHP does not pad out treatment plans unnecessarily — the goal is to get patients better and back to doing what they love as efficiently as possible.

## Content and Educational Resources

EHP publishes regular evidence-based content on injury management, rehabilitation, and performance for active adults. Topics covered include back pain management, rotator cuff rehabilitation, ACL recovery, running injury prevention, gym injury treatment, dry needling, and sports chiropractic.
